summary: On May 9, 2019, the Etobicoke York Panel of the Committee of Adjustment (the "Committee") approved an application brought by the owner of 90 Ash Crescent for a consent and related minor variances to sever the property into two undersized residential lots and to permit the construction of two new detached dwellings with garages on the newly created lots. On May 9, 2019, the Committee heard and approved the Consent and Variance Applications, subject to conditions. A copy of the Committee's decisions are attached. On May 1, 2019, Urban Forestry staff submitted a report recommending that the Applications be refused because the construction of the dwellings and driveway may require the removal of a healthy City owned multi-stemmed silver maple tree measuring 94cm in diameter. There has not been any information provided by the owner on how it would preserve the tree. The tree is a protected tree by Chapter 813, Article II Street Tree By-law. The Consent Application to sever the land into two undersized residential lots does not meet the provisions of Section 51(24) of the Planning Act, including, but not limited to, paragraph (c): whether the proposed severance conforms to the Official Plan. The removal of the Tree, as a result of the Consent Application, is contradictory to the natural environment policies of the Official Plan. The requested variances do not maintain the general…
decided: City Council on June 18 and 19, 2019, adopted the following: 1. City Council authorize the City Solicitor's appeal of May 29, 2019 and direct the City Solicitor and appropriate City Staff to attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body hearing to oppose the consent and variances requested in Applications B0063/17EYK, A0585/17EYK, and A0586/17EYK respecting 90 Ash Crescent. 2. City Council authorize the City Solicitor to negotiate a settlement of the appeal of the decision in Applications B0063/17EYK, A0585/17EYK, and A0586/17EYK respecting 90 Ash Crescent and authorize the City Solicitor to settle the matter on behalf of the City at the City Solicitor's discretion after consultation with the Ward Councillor and with the Director of Community Planning, Etobicoke York District.
